subject.title: [Bug]: Slack replies ~2s slower than other channels — dominant cost is Socket Mode event delivery; channel-side stalls fixed in #101888

question: Should Slack setup guidance explicitly recommend HTTP Request URLs for hosted/public-ingress deployments where reply latency matters, while keeping Socket Mode as the default for local or no-ingress hosts?
rationale: Current code already supports HTTP mode and current docs describe both transports, but changing the recommendation affects setup posture, security expectations, and the default mental model for Slack users.

options.title: Recommend HTTP for hosted Slack
options.body: Update Slack setup docs and any setup guidance to prefer HTTP Request URLs when public ingress is available and latency matters, while keeping Socket Mode for local/no-ingress deployments.

options.title: Keep transport guidance neutral
options.body: Leave docs as deployment-shape guidance only and accept that Socket Mode users may see the measured transport delay.

options.title: Ask for more canary proof first
options.body: Keep the issue open until a maintainer requests fresh HTTP-vs-Socket canary evidence before changing guidance.

recommendation.title: Recommend HTTP for hosted Slack
recommendation.body: Update Slack setup docs and any setup guidance to prefer HTTP Request URLs when public ingress is available and latency matters, while keeping Socket Mode for local/no-ingress deployments.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the recent Slack latency decomposition and merged fixes, so they are the clearest current owner for the remaining Slack transport recommendation.
